content:
Critics of rapper Nicki Minaj have something to say to the staunch Trump supporter after she dished out some advice to young voters during a Fox News appearance on Saturday.

Minaj, whose real name is Onika Tanya Maraj-Petty, spoke on "My View with Lara Trump," starting off what sounded like a fairly even-keeled take on the importance of voters exercising their right to vote.

Minaj said: "You know how much you want to have a say on what happens, and understand the only way to do that is to vote. Not just for president, but all local elections."

Minaj then urged voters to research the candidates in their area and make informed decisions.

"You are so blessed to be able to vote, and you must, more than ever, you must use the right that you have," Minaj said.

Had she stopped there, Minaj's words would have sounded like a middle-of-the-road message urging everyone to vote regardless of party — but the rapper then shattered that with a partisan rallying cry.

"Also, vote red [Republican]," Minaj said with a laugh.

Trump responded: "Amen, I think we can wrap her up; I have one more question. Nicki, wonderful sales pitch to the American voter, I love it."

Critics were quick to point out that Minaj is not a U.S. citizen, having been born in Trinidad and Tobago, and has no legal right to vote in American elections.

Others pointed out that young voters, even if they are conservative, generally do not watch Fox News. Some accused Minaj of trying to suck up to Trump in hopes of securing a presidential pardon for her brother Jelani Maraj, who was sentenced in 2017 to 25 years to life in prison on charges of predatory sexual assault of a child and endangering the welfare of a child.

It's worth noting that Maraj was convicted in Nassau County, New York under state law, and the president has no authority to pardon him.
